title: 第1190章 第一碎片第1189章 拼碎片的人
lines: 拼碎片的人带着卡拉斯往更深处走。碎片越来越稀，周围的虚空越来越空。不是碎片被清空了——是这片区域本来就没有多少碎片。
边荒的碎片飘了亿万年，早就形成了极乱极杂极混沌的分布，密集的地方碎片撞碎片，稀疏的地方碎片之间隔了很久很久的虚空。但这里不一样。
这里的碎片不是稀疏，是排列——极缓极慢极沉极重极古极老极韧极稳极静极柔极透极轻极未知地绕着同一个点转。不是被什么东西吸过去，是它们自己选择这么排列的。
它们绕着那个点转了亿万年，从来没有停过，也从来没有偏离过轨道。
核心悬着一片碎片。极薄极薄极薄，比他见过的任何碎片都薄。不像其他碎片那样有撕裂的边缘——它的边缘极光滑极完整极古老极陌生极未知，和万物之初那层大膜的表面一模一样。但它就是一片碎片。
它悬在所有碎片的中心，极缓极慢极沉极重极古极老极韧极稳极静极柔极透极轻极未知地自转着。每转一圈，周围那些碎片就极轻极轻极轻地震一下。
“边荒的第一片碎片。”拼碎片的人说，光丝在它背后极轻极轻极轻地飘着。“不是膜层分裂时扯下来的。膜层刚形成，还在冷却，它从膜层内部渗出来。第一滴渗出物。膜层那时候还是软的，它渗出来的时候裹着膜层最原始的温度。后来膜层冷却、裂开、分裂成亿万碎片，那些碎片全是撕裂的。只有它是完整的。它不是被撕下来的。它是自己渗出来的。边荒所有的碎片都是碎片，只有它是完整的碎片。”
卡拉斯走到那片碎片面前。碎片极薄极薄极薄，薄到能透过它看见后面的虚空。但它没有破，没有裂，没有碎。
它在边荒飘了亿万年，周围的碎片撞了亿万年，没有一片碎片敢撞它。不是畏惧，是它的存在方式和其他碎片完全不同——它是完整的。它不是碎片，它是膜层最初的模样。
他把壳片从怀里掏出来。壳片是膜层最近才自然脱落的完整壳片，和这片碎片同源。他把壳片贴在碎片表面，壳片极轻极轻极轻地一震。
碎片也极轻极轻极轻地一震。亿万年前膜层刚形成时渗出的第一滴，和亿万年后膜层自然脱落的壳片，两片完整的膜壳在边荒最深处碰在一起。
震波极轻极轻极轻极缓极慢极沉极重极古极老极韧极稳极静极柔极透极轻极未知。碎片表面的光滑膜面极轻极轻极轻地震着，振了很久才停。
震完之后，碎片表面裂开了一道极细极细极细的纹。不是被壳片震裂的，是它自己裂开的。
它等了亿万年，等另一片完整的东西来碰它。碰完之后它不需要再保持完整了，它可以裂开，让光透进去。裂口内部极亮极亮极亮，裹着极古极老极韧极稳极静极柔极透极轻极未知的光，和膜层最初的温度一模一样。
卡拉斯把手掌覆在那片碎片上，茧印贴着碎片表面那道极细极细极细的裂纹。他把铁城所有存在的名字一个一个报给它——膜层还完整，还在虚空深处悬着；壳片已经脱落，在拼碎片的人手里贴着；源匠旧铁轨从铁城铺到了膜层边缘；灶膛里三粒火星子并排烧着；冰层在写曲子；地心生出了轻劲；空庭有个幼崽刚学会坐。
所有从万物之初走出去的存在，全在。碎片极轻极轻极轻地震了一下，表面那道极细极细极细的裂纹里，光极轻极轻极轻地闪了一次。不是回应，是知道。它在这里飘了亿万年，第一次有人告诉它——你渗出去之后，外面有了这么多东西。

“我拼过它的碎片。”拼碎片的人忽然说。光丝在它背后极乱极杂极混沌地颤着。“它不是完整的。它也碎过。它从膜层渗出来的时候，裹着膜层最原始的温度，但它太薄太薄太薄，温度太高太高太高。膜层还在冷却，它已经渗出来了——温度把它自己烧裂了。它裂开的时候碎片溅出去，和边荒所有碎片都不一样，那些碎片是完整的碎片裂开的。它第一次裂开的时候，边荒还没有名字，还没有碎片，什么都没有。只有它。它裂开，碎片溅出去，后来又自己合拢。裂了合，合了裂。那些溅出去的碎片飘远了，再也合不回来。碎片和碎片之间隔着虚空，隔着时间，隔着它们自己。我拼过其中几片，拼的时候发现它们之间的接缝不需要磨丝——它们本来就是同一片碎片裂开的，接缝天生就能对上。我只用光丝把它们轻轻拉在一起，它们自己就合拢了。”
拼碎片的人停了一下，光丝在它背后极轻极轻极轻地飘着。它说现在知道了那些碎片是从哪里溅出去的，就是眼前这片第一碎片。
它裂开，碎片溅出去，溅出去的碎片飘了亿万年被它拼过几片。它一直不知道那些碎片为什么天生就能合拢，现在它站在第一碎片面前，知道了原因——因为它们从来没有真正分开过，它们是完整的一部分。
它拼碎片拼了这么久，拼的全是裂开的碎片。现在它找到了裂开的源头。它要把那些拼好的碎片还给第一碎片。
卡拉斯听完没有立刻回答。他把手掌从第一碎片表面收回来，从怀里掏出那些一路收集的碎片——膜层脱落的壳片，裹着冰层第一次推劲的旧碎片，封着初火火星子的更古碎片。
他把这些碎片并排放在第一碎片面前。碎片们极轻极轻极轻地震着，震法和第一碎片表面那道光纹的明灭完全同步。第一碎片裂开过，这些碎片也裂开过。
裂开的东西不需要拼回去——它们只是需要一个完整的东西告诉它们：你们的裂缝也能透光。
content_en:
The man who pieced together the pieces took Karas deeper. The fragments are getting thinner and thinner, and the surrounding void is getting emptier and emptier. It's not that the debris has been cleared - it's that there aren't many debris in this area to begin with.
The fragments in the borderlands have been floating for hundreds of millions of years, and have long formed a very chaotic and extremely chaotic distribution. The dense local fragments collide with each other, and the sparse local fragments are separated by a long, long void. But it's different here.
The fragments here are not sparse, but arranged - extremely slow, extremely slow, extremely heavy, extremely ancient, extremely old, extremely tough, extremely stable, extremely still, extremely soft, extremely transparent, extremely light, extremely light, and revolve around the same point unknown. It's not that they were sucked in by something, they chose to arrange themselves this way.
They circled that point for hundreds of millions of years, never stopping or deviating from their orbit.
A fragment hangs from the core. Very thin, very thin, thinner than any fragment he had ever seen. It doesn't have torn edges like other fragments - its edges are extremely smooth, intact, ancient, strange and unknown, exactly the same as the surface of the great membrane at the beginning of all things. But it's just a fragment.
It hangs in the center of all the fragments, extremely slow, extremely heavy, extremely ancient, extremely old, extremely tough, extremely stable, extremely quiet, extremely soft, extremely light, extremely light, extremely light, extremely spinning and spinning in an unknown way. Every time it turns around, the surrounding debris shakes very lightly.
"The first fragment of the wilderness." The person who pieced it together said, and the light thread floated very lightly behind it. "It was not torn off when the film split. The film had just formed and was still cooling. It seeped out from inside the film. The first drop of exudate. The film was still soft at that time, and it was wrapped in the original temperature of the film when it seeped out. Later, the film cooled, cracked, and split into billions of fragments, and those fragments were all torn. Only it is complete. It was not torn off. It seeped out by itself. All the fragments in the border wilderness are fragments, and only it is a complete fragment."
Karas walked over to the fragment. The fragment is extremely thin, extremely thin, so thin that you can see the void behind it through it. But it wasn't broken, it wasn't cracked, it wasn't shattered.
It floated in the wilderness for hundreds of millions of years, and the surrounding debris collided with it for hundreds of millions of years, but no one dared to hit it. It's not that it's fearful, it's that its way of existence is completely different from other fragments - it's complete. It's not a fragment, it's the original appearance of the membrane.
He took the shell pieces out of his arms. The shell fragment is a complete shell fragment whose membrane has recently fallen off naturally, and has the same origin as this fragment. He put the shell piece against the surface of the fragment, and the shell piece shook very lightly.
The fragments also shook very lightly. The first drop that oozed out when the membrane layer was first formed hundreds of millions of years ago, and the shell pieces that naturally fell off hundreds of millions of years later, the two complete membrane shells collided together in the deepest part of the wilderness.
The shock wave is extremely light, extremely light, extremely light, extremely slow, extremely slow, extremely heavy, extremely heavy, extremely ancient, extremely old, extremely tough, extremely stable, extremely static, extremely soft, extremely transparent, extremely light, extremely unknown. The smooth membrane on the surface of the fragment vibrated very lightly, very lightly, and it vibrated for a long time before stopping.
After the earthquake, a very fine, very fine crack appeared on the surface of the fragment. It wasn't cracked by the shell, it was cracked by itself.
It waited for eons for another whole piece to touch it. It no longer needs to stay intact after being touched, it can crack and let light in. The inside of the crack is extremely bright, extremely bright, extremely bright, wrapped in extremely ancient, extremely old, extremely tough, extremely stable, extremely static, extremely soft, extremely light, extremely light and unknown light, exactly the same as the initial temperature of the film.
Karas put his palm on the fragment, and the cocoon mark was against the very fine, very fine crack on the surface of the fragment. He told it the names of all the existences in the Iron City one by one - the membrane was still intact and still hanging in the depths of the void; the shell fragments had fallen off and were attached to the hands of the people who were piecing the pieces together; the old railway tracks from the original craftsman were laid from the Iron City to the edge of the membrane; three sparks were burning side by side in the stove; the ice layer was writing music; there was lightness in the center of the earth; there was a cub in the empty garden who had just learned to sit.
All existences that have gone out from the beginning of all things exist. The fragments shook very lightly, and light flashed very lightly in the very fine cracks on the surface. Not responding, but knowing. It has been floating here for hundreds of millions of years, and for the first time someone told it that after you seep out, there are so many things outside.
"I have pieced it together." The person who pieced it together suddenly said. The light threads trembled chaotically behind it. "It is not complete. It has also broken. When it seeped out of the film, it was wrapped with the original temperature of the film, but it was too thin, too thin, too thin, and the temperature was too high. The film was still cooling, and it had seeped out - the temperature burned itself. When it cracked, the fragments splashed out. It was different from all the fragments in Bianhuang. Those fragments were broken by complete fragments. When it cracked for the first time, Bianhuang had no name, no fragments, nothing. Just. There is it. It split, the fragments flew out, and then they closed up. The scattered fragments drifted away and never came back. There was a gap between the fragments, separated by time. When I pieced together some of them, I found that the seams between them were originally the same fragments, and the seams were naturally aligned. "
The person piecing together the fragments paused for a moment, and the light thread floated very lightly behind it. It said that it now knew where those fragments splashed out, which was the first fragment in front of it.
It cracked, and the fragments flew out. The fragments that flew out were pieced together by it after hundreds of millions of years. It has never known why those fragments were born to come together. Now it stands in front of the first fragment and knows the reason - because they have never really been separated, they are a complete part.
It took so long to piece it together, and all it ended up in were cracked pieces. Now it found the source of the crack. It's about giving back the pieces that have been put together
